lanes.name: notifications
lanes.note: The estate's only live Amex source. Went silent 57.1 h on 2026-07-29 (flat phone). RETIRED 2026-08-15: the amex-alert-detail lane (>=50% of Amex alerts must carry an amount) lived here and was removed. It did its job — it caught the 2026-08-06 changepoint after which Amex push alerts carry no amount or merchant — but that is now a PERMANENT state, so the check was asserting something nobody expects to be true again and fired hourly for six days. The open work is tracked as issue i-20260814-154101 (mo.lan/issues). Arrival of the notifications themselves is still guarded by this lane. Re-add a check here only to detect the amounts COMING BACK, which needs an inverted predicate this checker does not have today.

lanes.name: ultrahuman
lanes.note:
Ring data. `date` is written by the fetcher's own loop, so an empty 200 still yields a dated row — without `require` this lane reads ok on a table with no measurement in it. The four fields are payload-borne and independent: hr_points alone would be too strict (20 of 143 real days have none while still carrying steps/vo2_max). Coverage collapse is a separate problem, held by ultrahuman-coverage.

`active_minutes` was a fifth certifier and was REMOVED 2026-08-21: it is non-null on days whose payload carries no hr, no temp, no hrv and no steps series and an empty Sleep object, so it certified rows containing no measurement. Measured over the 154 rows of that date's artifact: it was the sole require-satisfying field on exactly 11 rows (2026-06-03..06-11, 2026-08-18..08-19), all with hr_points=0, and on none of the rows that carry samples — across the 95 payloads with samples and active_minutes>0 the steps series is never empty (min 87 points). So dropping it removes 11 false certifications and loses no true one, and it moves this lane's newest data-carrying row from 2026-08-19 to 2026-08-17, the last day with any samples. Whether the partner API echoes, extrapolates or measures active_minutes on those days was NOT established and does not matter here — the field stays in the artifact, it just no longer counts as proof the ring reported. Same class as the night_rhr echo closed in ea378fe.

lanes.name: technogym-cardio
lanes.note: Generous window: no training is indistinguishable from a stalled fetch.

lanes.name: ultrahuman-coverage
lanes.note:
Does a night carry enough HR samples to be worth reading? The ring is worn AT NIGHT ONLY -- deliberate, confirmed by the operator 2026-08-23 ("I rarely wear it during day except if I forget to take it off") -- so any 24 h-shaped test measures his habits, not the data.

That is what the previous predicate did. It required hr_span_h >= 12, and hr_span_h is FIRST-TO-LAST: a night-only wearer scores ~23.9 h when he puts the ring on before midnight (one point at 23:5x, one at 07:00, a 12.8 h hole between) and ~7 h when he puts it on after. So the lane was reporting what time he went to bed. It fired on 2026-08-21 at 5/9 against a 0.6 floor while every night in the window had a complete sleep summary and a normal ~110-point HR series -- an alarm about nothing, of the kind you learn to ignore. See moprox-memory/ultrahuman-span-is-not-coverage.

hr_points >= 40 tests DENSITY instead, which is what 'usable' means here, and it separates cleanly. Measured over the whole 156-row archive on 2026-08-23:
  Apr 0.87 | May 0.87 | Jun 0.43 | Jul 0.81 | Aug 1.00   (floor 0.6)
June is the real coverage collapse (median 19 hr_points, 16 nights with no sleep at all) and it fails by a wide margin; every healthy month clears the floor with room; the current 10-day window is 10/10. The old predicate scored Apr 0.80 / May 0.71 / Jun 0.27 / Jul 0.74 / Aug 0.91 -- it caught June too, but it was catching bedtime everywhere else.

40 rather than 60: 60 also works (Aug 0.96, Jun 0.37) but costs a night like 2026-08-17 (67 points, 8.6 min max gap -- a short but perfectly clean night) for nothing. `where` is unchanged and is inert: hr_span_h is non-null on all 19 zero-HR rows, so nothing is filtered out either way; it stays as documentation of intent. Row PRESENCE is the sibling `ultrahuman` lane's job, not this one's.

STILL NOT GUARDED, on purpose: hr_cov_5m and hr_gap_max_min, the interior view. Both are backfilled over the whole archive, and both are dominated by the deliberate daytime hole (median longest gap 12.8 h since July, ~2 h in April-May), so any floor over them measures wear habit again. If daytime wear ever becomes the norm, they are the right fields -- not this one.
